newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DG Bank seen sharpening Hungary banking competiton.
newsitem.headline: DG Bank seen sharpening Hungary banking competiton.

text.p: The acquisition of Hungary's Takarekbank by Germany's DG Bank will sharpen competition for the country's retail banking market and may cut the market share of some large retail banks, analysts said on Thursday.
"Those banks which have begun fighting for cheap retail custom will be affected the most," said Zoltan Varadi of Daewoo Securities'.

A consortium of DG Bank and Hungaria Biztosito, the Hungarian insurance unit of Germany's Allianz, won a privatisation tender on Wednesday for a 60.98 percent stake in Takarekbank, umbrella bank of Hungary's savings cooperatives.
The stake of DG Bank will be 55.98 percent.
The purchase price for the whole 60.98 percent stake in Takarekbank, which has registered capital of 1.34 billion forints, was 41.3 million German marks.

The price, 531 percent of the face value, was unprecedentedly high in Hungarian bank privatisations, Takarekbank officials said, while analysts added that Takarekbank was made valuable by the large network and clientele of the savings cooperatives.

Hungarian savings cooperatives have some two million retail customers and a network of more than 1,600 branches, mainly in smaller towns and villages where other financial services are only available in post offices.
The savings cooperatives, which hold a 33 percent stake in Takarekbank, and their umbrella bank are the fifth largest banking group in Hungary by assets.

"Savings cooperatives in small towns have a very strong ability to collect deposits as there are hardly any other financial services there," said Peter Postenyi of Raiffeisen Securities. "With more services new clients can also be won."
The investors undertook to raise Takarekbank's registered capital to two billion forints in six months, buying the new shares at 200 percent of their face value.
Takarekbank said on Wednesday it expected DG Bank to modernise the savings cooperatives, improve their services and help them expand their retail market share.

"DG bank has the experience as it is a savings cooperative bank, just like Takarekbank," said Postyeni. "With a capital increase and better infrastructure a market share increase seems to be realistic."
However, DG Bank would have to face strong competitors in Hungary, analysts said.
As conquering new positions in an already very competitive enterprise market was difficult, more and more banks were turning towards individual banking, they said.
They were prepared to carry out expensive developments as Hungary foresaw strong economic growth over the next few years, heralding the expansion of the retail market, analysts said.

Two Dutch banks, ABN-Amro and ING, which recently purchased banks from the Hungarian state, were both looking at retail banking and were eager to prise away market share from the two largest retail banks, OTP and Postabank, analysts added.
They said the strengthening of Takarekbank's positions would increase competition mainly with Postabank.

"OTP is in a better position as its portfolio is more diverse, it has more entrepreneurs as clients," Varadi said. "But many of Postabank's branches, in post offices, are not as professional as savings cooperatives."
Postabank deputy CEO Robert Muranyi told Reuters that they were not afraid of the competition of Takarekbank.
"We always had to face competition, and our competitors, like OTP are already there in post offices," he said.
Analysts said that DG Bank's presence in Hungary and the further sharpening competition would benefit retail banking clients as it would lead to an improvement in services.

"This is part of the on-going process that several major international investors are acquiring major stakes in Hungarian banks," said James Oates, director at UBS in London. "The Hungarian financial system needs more capital".
He added that even if DG Bank was ambitious to boost Takarekbank's market share, it would take time.
"I don't think (Takarekbank's sale) will have a dramatic effect straight away."
